problem.title: Trim or Tile?
problem.statement: A rectangular floor is 4 meters long and 3 meters wide. How much trim is needed around its edge, and how many square meters of tile cover it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 7 m of trim and 12 m² of tile

choices.label: B
choices.text: 12 m of trim and 14 m² of tile

choices.label: C
choices.text: 14 m of trim and 12 m² of tile

choices.label: D
choices.text: 24 m of trim and 7 m² of tile

hints: Trace all four sides for trim.
Count rows times columns for tile coverage.

validationMethods: direct boundary and array calculations: 2(4+3)=14 and 4(3)=12
independent unit audit distinguishes linear trim from square tile; option audit

problem.title: One Rectangle, Two Measures
problem.statement: A rectangle is 11 cm by 4 cm. What are its perimeter and area, respectively?

validationMethods: formula derivation from side sum and array product
independent unit-and-option audit: only B pairs 30 linear with 44 square

problem.title: Name the Coverage
problem.statement: A rectangular carpet is 7 yards long and 5 yards wide. Which measurement correctly describes its area?
hints: Multiply the side lengths and preserve the dimensional unit.

solutionSteps.title: Count square yards
solutionSteps.body: 7 × 5 = 35, and each counted unit is a one-yard square, so the area is 35 yd².

validationMethods: unit-square array: seven columns times five rows is 35 squares
dimensional audit rejects linear-unit choice C despite matching number

problem.title: Same Boundary, New Coverage
problem.statement: A 2-by-8 rectangle and a 5-by-5 square have the same perimeter. How much greater is the square's area?
hints: Then compare the two area products.

validationMethods: independent unit-square difference 25-16=9 and option audit

problem.title: Which Height Counts?
problem.statement: A triangle has base 12 units, perpendicular height 5 units, and a slanted side 7 units. What is its area?
hints: Use the length perpendicular to the chosen base.
Take half of base times height.

solutionSteps.title: Choose true height
solutionSteps.body: The perpendicular height is 5, not the slanted side 7.

validationMethods: independent doubling check: two triangles fill area-60 parallelogram; distractor and unit audit

problem.title: Preserve the Tiles
problem.statement: A 6-by-6 square is rearranged into a rectangle with whole-number side lengths 4 and x but the same area. What are x and the new rectangle's perimeter?
hints: Then trace the new rectangle's four sides.

validationMethods: equal-area equation 4x=36 gives x=9 and side-sum perimeter 26
independent tile factorization 36=4·9 plus direct boundary sum 4+9+4+9=26; choices audited
